verses.sloka: निविष्टायां तु सेनायामुत्सुको भरतस्तदा।जगाम भ्रातरं द्रष्टुं शत्रुध्नमनुदर्शयन् ॥ २.९९.१॥
verses.transliteration: niviṣṭāyāṁ tu senāyāmutsuko bharatastadā।jagāma bhrātaraṁ draṣṭuṁ śatrudhnamanudarśayan ॥ 2.99.1॥

translations.english: Eager to see his brother, Bharata encamped the army and set out showing the hermitage to Satrughna.
translations.hindi: कुलधम:--प्रजापालन । (गो० ) Vin ०पश्चनवतिहम $/8 सग?” onations अथ शेलाद्विनिष्क्रम्य मैथिलीं कोसलेरप्ररः । अदर्शयच्छुभजलां रम्यां मन्दाकिनीं नदीम्‌

verses.sloka: ऋषिं वसिष्ठं सन्दिश्य मातऽर्मे शीघ्रमानय।इति त्वरितमग्रे स जगाम गुरुवत्सल: ॥ २.९९.२॥
verses.transliteration: ṛṣiṁ vasiṣṭhaṁ sandiśya māta'rme śīghramānaya।iti tvaritamagre sa jagāma guruvatsala: ॥ 2.99.2॥

translations.english: Bharata, deeply devoted towards elders, indicated to sage Vasistha to bring along the mothers, and proceeded ahead quickly.
translations.hindi: कमलनयन श्रीरामचन्द्र चन्द्रमा के समान सुन्दर सुखवाली स्त्रियां मै श्रेष्ठ जनकतनया से बोले

verses.sloka: सुमन्त्रस्त्वपि शत्रुघ्नमदूरादन्वपद्यत।रामदर्शनजस्तर्षो भरतस्येव तस्य च ॥ २.९९.३॥
verses.transliteration: sumantrastvapi śatrughnamadūrādanvapadyata।rāmadarśanajastarṣo bharatasyeva tasya ca ॥ 2.99.3॥

translations.english: Sumantra, who was overeager, like Bharata, to see Rama, followed Satrughna who was not far from him.
translations.hindi: हे वैदेही ! इस विचित्र तटं वाली, रमणीय और हंस सारसादि पत्तियों से सेवित मन्दाकिनी नदी को देखो

verses.sloka: गच्छन्नेवाथ भरतस्तापसालयसंस्थिताम्।भ्रातु: पर्णकुटीं श्रीमानुटजं च ददर्श ह ॥ २.९९.४॥
verses.transliteration: gacchannevātha bharatastāpasālayasaṁsthitām।bhrātu: parṇakuṭīṁ śrīmānuṭajaṁ ca dadarśa ha ॥ 2.99.4॥

translations.english: While walking, Bharata beheld a hut made of leaves looking like a hermit's cottage.
translations.hindi: इस नदी के उभय तट फल फूल वाले अनेक जाति के वृर्छो से परिपूर्ण हैं । उनसे इस नदी की शोभा वैसी ही हो रही है जैसी कि कुवेर की सौगन्धिका नाम्नी नदी की

verses.sloka: शालायास्त्वग्रतस्तस्या ददर्श भरतस्तदा।काष्ठानि चावभग्नानि पुष्पाण्युपचितानि च ॥ २.९९.५॥
verses.transliteration: śālāyāstvagratastasyā dadarśa bharatastadā।kāṣṭhāni cāvabhagnāni puṣpāṇyupacitāni ca ॥ 2.99.5॥

translations.english: In front of that hut Bharata beheld shattered logs of wood and also flowers plucked.
translations.hindi: इस नदी के सव घाट'बड़े रमणीय हैं । अतः वहाँ जा कर स्नान करने की मेरी इच्छा हो रही हे । अभी मृगो के फुड इन घाटों पर जल पी कर गए हैं। अतः वहाँ का जल गँदला हो रहा है

verses.sloka: सलक्ष्मणस्य रामस्य ददर्शाश्रममीयुष:।कृतं वृक्षेष्वभिज्ञानं कुशचीरै: क्वचित् क्वचित् ॥ २.९९.६॥
verses.transliteration: salakṣmaṇasya rāmasya dadarśāśramamīyuṣa:।kṛtaṁ vṛkṣeṣvabhijñānaṁ kuśacīrai: kvacit kvacit ॥ 2.99.6॥

translations.english: Bharata beheld here and there knots of kusa grass and strips of bark tied on trees as signs to ascertain the way to the hermitage of Rama and Lakshmana.
translations.hindi: हे प्रिये ! देखो, जटा और मृगचर्म धारण किए और वृक्षों की छाल पहिने हुए ऋषि लोग, इस नदी में यथासमय स्नान करते हैँ

verses.sloka: ददर्श च वने तस्मिन् महत: सञ्चयान् कृतान्।मृगाणां महिषाणां च कऺरीषै: शीतकारणात् ॥ २.९९.७॥
verses.transliteration: dadarśa ca vane tasmin mahata: sañcayān kṛtān।mṛgāṇāṁ mahiṣāṇāṁ ca kaऺrīṣai: śītakāraṇāt ॥ 2.99.7॥

translations.english: He also beheld large heaps of dried cakes of dung of buffaloes and deer for use against cold in the forest.
translations.hindi: हे विशालाक्षि ! इस ओर ये सब तीक्षण नियमों का पालन करने वाले मुनिगण नियमानुसार ऊपर को बाँह उठा कर सूर्य अगवान का उपस्थान कर रहे हें

verses.sloka: गच्छन्नेव महाबाहुर्द्युतिमान् भरतस्तदा।शत्रुघ्नं चाब्रवीद्धृष्टस्तानमात्यांश्च सर्वश: ॥ २.९९.८॥
verses.transliteration: gacchanneva mahābāhurdyutimān bharatastadā।śatrughnaṁ cābravīddhṛṣṭastānamātyāṁśca sarvaśa: ॥ 2.99.8॥

translations.english: Walking on, the longarmed, effulgent and delighted Bharata said to Satrughna and the ministers surrounding him:
translations.hindi: देखो पवन से कम्पित इन वृक्षा के हिलने से यह पत्र'त eS तव्रताः-तीच्णनियमाः । ( गो० ) ५ मारुतोद्ध,त शिखरै:--वायु- कम्पितशाखैः । ( गो० ) | पुष्प गिरते हैँ उनसे चित्रकूट पर्वत मानों नदी को पुष्पाञ्जलि रहा है

verses.sloka: मन्ये प्राप्ता: स्म तं देशं भरद्वाजो यमब्रवीत्।नातिदूरे हि मन्येऽहं नदीं मन्दाकिनीमित: ॥ २.९९.९॥
verses.transliteration: manye prāptā: sma taṁ deśaṁ bharadvājo yamabravīt।nātidūre hi manye'haṁ nadīṁ mandākinīmita: ॥ 2.99.9॥

translations.english: We must have reached the region about which Bharadwaja had spoken. I think river Mandakini is not far from here.

verses.sloka: उच्चैर्बद्धानि चीराणि लक्ष्मणेन भवेदयम्।अभिज्ञानकृत: पन्था विकाले गन्तुमिच्छता ॥ २.९९.१०॥
verses.transliteration: uccairbaddhāni cīrāṇi lakṣmaṇena bhavedayam।abhijñānakṛta: panthā vikāle gantumicchatā ॥ 2.99.10॥

translations.english: Here are long bark garments fastened on lofty places as marks of identification left by Lakshmana, to locate the path at odd times which may be needed while going out.
translations.hindi: हे भद्रे ! वायु के मोकों में नदी के तट पर हट हुए पुष्पों के हेर को देखो । जो फूल जल में उड़ कर जा गिरे हैं, वे पानी पर कैसे उतरा रहे हैं, उन्हें भी तुम देखो

verses.sloka: इदं चोदात्तदन्तानां कुञ्जराणां तरस्विनाम्।शैलपार्श्वे परिक्रान्तमन्योन्यमभिगर्जताम् ॥ २.९९.११॥
verses.transliteration: idaṁ codāttadantānāṁ kuñjarāṇāṁ tarasvinām।śailapārśve parikrāntamanyonyamabhigarjatām ॥ 2.99.11॥

translations.english: This must be the place on the hillside on which mighty tuskers wander about trumpeting and charging at one another.
translations.hindi: हे कल्याणि ! फूलों के ढेरों पर चढ़े हुए चक्रवाक्र रति के लिए अपनी मादाओं को बुलाने के हेतु कैसी मधुर बोली बोल रहे हैं

verses.sloka: यमेवाधातुमिच्छन्ति तापसा: सततं वने।तस्यासौ दृश्यते धूम: सङ्कुल: कृष्णवर्त्मन: ॥ २.९९.१२॥
verses.transliteration: yamevādhātumicchanti tāpasā: satataṁ vane।tasyāsau dṛśyate dhūma: saṅkula: kṛṣṇavartmana: ॥ 2.99.12॥

translations.english: Here is the thick smoke emanating from the blacktrailed fire maintained perpetually by the ascetics living in the forest.

verses.sloka: अत्राहं पुरुषव्याघ्रं गुरुसंस्कारकारिणम्।आर्यं द्रक्ष्यामि संहृष्टो महर्षिमिव राघवम् ॥ २.९९.१३॥
verses.transliteration: atrāhaṁ puruṣavyāghraṁ gurusaṁskārakāriṇam।āryaṁ drakṣyāmi saṁhṛṣṭo maharṣimiva rāghavam ॥ 2.99.13॥

translations.english: I shall see here with a delighted heart the venerable Rama, the best of men, who renders great hospitality (to elders) and who resembles a maharshi.
translations.hindi: हे सीते ! अब तुम इस मन्दाकिनी नदी में, जिसमें शम, दम और तप से यक्त एवं पापरहित लिद्रलोग नित्य स्नान किआ करते हैं, चल कर मेरे साथ स्नान करो

verses.sloka: अथ गत्वा मुहूर्तं तु चित्रकूटं स राघव:।मन्दाकिनीमनुप्राप्तस्तं जनं चेदमब्रवीत् ॥ २.९९.१४॥
verses.transliteration: atha gatvā muhūrtaṁ tu citrakūṭaṁ sa rāghava:।mandākinīmanuprāptastaṁ janaṁ cedamabravīt ॥ 2.99.14॥

translations.english: Bharata walked for a short distance towards mount Chitrkuta when he reached river Mandakini. And then said to his ministers:
translations.hindi: हे सीते ! तुम जैसे अपनी सखियों के साथ निःशङ्क जलक्रीड़ा करतीं थीं, वैसे ही मेरे साथ भी इस मंदाकिनी में लाल सफेद कसल के फूलों को डुवोती हुई जलक्रीडा करो

verses.sloka: जगत्यां पुरुषव्याघ्र आस्ते वीरासने रत:।जनेन्द्रो निर्जनं प्राप्य धिङ्मे जन्म सजीवितम् ॥ २.९९.१५॥
verses.transliteration: jagatyāṁ puruṣavyāghra āste vīrāsane rata:।janendro nirjanaṁ prāpya dhiṅme janma sajīvitam ॥ 2.99.15॥

translations.english: Rama, the lord of men, a tiger among men, is sitting on the ground in a 'heroic' (yogic) posture in this secluded forest. O fie upon my birth and my life
translations.hindi: टिप्पणी--लाल सफेद कमल के फूलों से भूषणटीकाकार ने यह अभिप्राय बतलाया है-- स्तनजघनाघातजनिततरद्धे रितिभावः किन्तु शिरोमणिटीकाकार का कथन है कि, क्रीड़ा के लिए लाल सफेद रंग के कमलों से मंदाकिनी के जल को ढक दो | त्वं पौरजनवद्‌“द्वयालानयोध्यामिव पर्वतम्‌ | मन्यस्व वनिते नित्यं सरयूवदिमां नदीस्‌

verses.sloka: मत्कृते व्यसनं प्राप्तो लोकनाथो महाद्युति:।सर्वान् कामान् परित्यज्य वने वसति राघव: ॥ २.९९.१६॥
verses.transliteration: matkṛte vyasanaṁ prāpto lokanātho mahādyuti:।sarvān kāmān parityajya vane vasati rāghava: ॥ 2.99.16॥

translations.english: Effulgent Rama, the lord of the world, had to renounce all desires and undergo this calamity of living in the forest on my account.
translations.hindi: हे वैदेही ! यह धर्मात्मा लक्ष्मण मेरे आज्ञाकारी हैं और तुम भी सदा मेरी आज्ञा के अनुसार काम किया करती हो । इससे सुके बड़ी प्रसन्नता होती है

verses.sloka: इति लोकसमाक्रुष्ट: पादेष्वद्य प्रसादयन्।रामस्य निपतिष्यामि सीताया लक्ष्मणस्य च ॥ २.९९.१७॥
verses.transliteration: iti lokasamākruṣṭa: pādeṣvadya prasādayan।rāmasya nipatiṣyāmi sītāyā lakṣmaṇasya ca ॥ 2.99.17॥

translations.english: Reviled by the world, I shall now fall at the feet of Sita, Rama and Lakshmana seeking their grace.
translations.hindi: त्रिकाल स्नान और तुम्हारे ' साथ मधु मूल और फल का ` भोजन करता हुआ, मैं, अयोध्या के बास की और राज्य की आकांक्षा नहीं करता

verses.sloka: एवं स विलपंस्तस्मिन् वने दशरथात्मज:।ददर्श महतीं पुण्यां पर्णशालां मनोरमाम् ॥ २.९९.१८॥
verses.transliteration: evaṁ sa vilapaṁstasmin vane daśarathātmaja:।dadarśa mahatīṁ puṇyāṁ parṇaśālāṁ manoramām ॥ 2.99.18॥

translations.english: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.
translations.hindi: जो गर्जो के यूथों से युक्त है और जिसका जल हाथी, सिंह ओर बंदर पिया करते हैं, उस रमणीय एव सुन्दर पुष्पां से यक्त वृक्षों द्वारा शोभित मंदाकिनी नदी का सेवन कर, वह कौन पुरुष है जो दुःखी से छट, सुखी न हो ?

verses.sloka: सालतालाश्वकर्णानां पर्णैर्बहुभिरावृताम्।विशालां मृदुभिस्तीर्णां कुशैर्वेदिमिवाध्वरे ॥ २.९९.१९॥
verses.transliteration: sālatālāśvakarṇānāṁ parṇairbahubhirāvṛtām।viśālāṁ mṛdubhistīrṇāṁ kuśairvedimivādhvare ॥ 2.99.19॥

verses.sloka: शक्रायुधनिकाशैश्च कार्मुकैर्भारसाधनै:।रुक्मपृष्टष्ठैर्महासारै: शोभितां शत्रुबाधकै: ॥ २.९९.२०॥
verses.transliteration: śakrāyudhanikāśaiśca kārmukairbhārasādhanai:।rukmapṛṣṭaṣṭhairmahāsārai: śobhitāṁ śatrubādhakai: ॥ 2.99.20॥

verses.sloka: अर्करश्मिप्रतीकाशैर्घोरैस्तूणीगतै: शरै:।शोभितां दीप्तवदनै: सर्प्पैर्भोगवतीमिव ॥ २.९९.२१॥
verses.transliteration: arkaraśmipratīkāśairghoraistūṇīgatai: śarai:।śobhitāṁ dīptavadanai: sarppairbhogavatīmiva ॥ 2.99.21॥

verses.sloka: महारजतवासोभ्यामसिभ्यां च विराजिताम्।रुक्मबिन्दुविचित्राभ्यां चर्मभ्यां चापि शोभिताम् ॥ २.९९.२२॥
verses.transliteration: mahārajatavāsobhyāmasibhyāṁ ca virājitām।rukmabinduvicitrābhyāṁ carmabhyāṁ cāpi śobhitām ॥ 2.99.22॥

translations.english: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.

verses.sloka: गोधाङ्गुलित्रैरासक्तैश्चित्रै: काञ्चनभूषितै:।अरिसङ्घैरनाधृष्यां मृगै: सिंहगुहामिव ॥ २.९९.२३॥
verses.transliteration: godhāṅgulitrairāsaktaiścitrai: kāñcanabhūṣitai:।arisaṅghairanādhṛṣyāṁ mṛgai: siṁhaguhāmiva ॥ 2.99.23॥

translations.english: Lamenting in this way Bharata beheld in that forest an excellent, sacred and enchanting hut covered with a lot of leaves of sala, palmyra and aswakarna trees like a sacrificial altar spread with soft kusa grass. Goldplated bows that resembled the thunderbolt of Indra, powerful and capable of achieving great targets and oppressing the enemies, adorned the hut. Arrows glittering like the rays of the Sun, were dreadful, with blazing heads and stored in quivers adorned it like the hooded serpents illumining the city of Bhogavati (in the nether world). A pair of swords in scabbards made of excellent silver, two shields of different colours with golden spots, fingerguards made of skin of iguana decorated with gold were hanging there. It was impregnable to enemy hordes like the cave of a lion to the deer.

verses.sloka: प्रागुदक्प्रवणां वेदिं विशालां दीप्तपावकाम्।ददर्श भरतस्तत्र पुण्यां रामनिवेशने ॥ २.९९.२४॥
verses.transliteration: prāgudakpravaṇāṁ vediṁ viśālāṁ dīptapāvakām।dadarśa bharatastatra puṇyāṁ rāmaniveśane ॥ 2.99.24॥

translations.english: Bharata beheld at Rama's residence a sacred and spacious altar sloping to the northeast, with a burning fire upon it.

verses.sloka: निरीक्ष्य स मुहूर्त्तं तु ददर्श भरतो गुरम्।उटजे राममासीनं जटामण्डलधारिणम् ॥ २.९९.२५॥
verses.transliteration: nirīkṣya sa muhūrttaṁ tu dadarśa bharato guram।uṭaje rāmamāsīnaṁ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam ॥ 2.99.25॥

translations.english: Bharata looked around for a moment and saw his esteemed brother Rama seated in that thatched cottage wearing matted locks of hair.

verses.sloka: तं तु कृष्णाजिनधरं चीरवल्कलवाससम्।ददर्श राममासीनमभित: पावकोपमम् ॥ २.९९.२६॥
verses.transliteration: taṁ tu kṛṣṇājinadharaṁ cīravalkalavāsasam।dadarśa rāmamāsīnamabhita: pāvakopamam ॥ 2.99.26॥

translations.english: He saw Rama, lord of the oceanbound earth, seated like blazing fire, clad in antelope skin and garment of bark, with long arms and shoulders like a lion and eyes like white lotuses. The mightyarmed warrior seemed like Brahma, the creator and the eternal, protector of righteousness. Accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana Rama sat on the bare ground strewn with darbha grass.

verses.sloka: सिंहस्कन्धं महाबाहुं पुण्डरीकनिभेक्षणम्।पृथिव्या: सागरान्ताया भर्त्तारं धर्मचारिणम् ॥ २.९९.२७॥
verses.transliteration: siṁhaskandhaṁ mahābāhuṁ puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇam।pṛthivyā: sāgarāntāyā bharttāraṁ dharmacāriṇam ॥ 2.99.27॥

translations.english: He saw Rama, lord of the oceanbound earth, seated like blazing fire, clad in antelope skin and garment of bark, with long arms and shoulders like a lion and eyes like white lotuses. The mightyarmed warrior seemed like Brahma, the creator and the eternal, protector of righteousness. Accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana Rama sat on the bare ground strewn with darbha grass.

verses.sloka: उपविष्टं महाबाहुं ब्रह्माणमिव शाश्वतम्।स्थण्डिले दर्भसंस्तीर्णे सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च ॥ २.९९.२८॥
verses.transliteration: upaviṣṭaṁ mahābāhuṁ brahmāṇamiva śāśvatam।sthaṇḍile darbhasaṁstīrṇe sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca ॥ 2.99.28॥

translations.english: He saw Rama, lord of the oceanbound earth, seated like blazing fire, clad in antelope skin and garment of bark, with long arms and shoulders like a lion and eyes like white lotuses. The mightyarmed warrior seemed like Brahma, the creator and the eternal, protector of righteousness. Accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana Rama sat on the bare ground strewn with darbha grass.

verses.sloka: तं दृष्ट्वा भरत: श्रीमान् दु:खशोकपरिप्लुत:।अभ्यधावत धर्मात्मा भरत: कैकयीसुत: ॥ २.९९.२९॥
verses.transliteration: taṁ dṛṣṭvā bharata: śrīmān du:khaśokaparipluta:।abhyadhāvata dharmātmā bharata: kaikayīsuta: ॥ 2.99.29॥

translations.english: Beholding Rama, Bharata the majestic and righteous son of Kaikeyi overwhelmed with grief and distress rushed towards him.

verses.sloka: दृष्ट्वैव विललापार्त्तो बाष्पसन्दिग्धया गिरा।अशक्नुवन् धारयितुं धैर्याद्वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ २.९९.३०॥
verses.transliteration: dṛṣṭvaiva vilalāpārtto bāṣpasandigdhayā girā।aśaknuvan dhārayituṁ dhairyādvacanamabravīt ॥ 2.99.30॥

translations.english: On seeing Rama, Bharata could not control his grief with patience and lamented in great anguish and with words choked with tears said:

verses.sloka: य: संसदि प्रकृतिभिर्भवेद्युक्त उपासितुम्।वन्यैर्मृगैरुपासीन: सोऽयमास्ते ममाग्रज: ॥ २.९९.३१॥
verses.transliteration: ya: saṁsadi prakṛtibhirbhavedyukta upāsitum।vanyairmṛgairupāsīna: so'yamāste mamāgraja: ॥ 2.99.31॥

translations.english: My elder brother who deserves to be attended by ministers and other subjects in the royal assembly sits here today in the forest surrounded by wild beasts.

verses.sloka: वासोभिर्बहुसाहस्रैर्यो महात्मा पुरोचित:।मृगाजिने सोऽयमिह प्रवस्ते धर्ममाचरन् ॥ २.९९.३२॥
verses.transliteration: vāsobhirbahusāhasrairyo mahātmā purocita:।mṛgājine so'yamiha pravaste dharmamācaran ॥ 2.99.32॥

translations.english: Such magnanimous Rama, a follower of dharma, accustomed to be attired in thousands of dresses in the past now clad in two deer skins, is practising righteousness.

verses.sloka: अधारयद्यो विविधाश्चित्रा: सुमनसस्तदा सोऽयं जटाभारमिमं वहते राघव: कथम् ॥ २.९९.३३॥
verses.transliteration: adhārayadyo vividhāścitrā: sumanasastadā so'yaṁ jaṭābhāramimaṁ vahate rāghava: katham ॥ 2.99.33॥

translations.english: How is it that Rama who used to wear variegated flowers formerly, now bears these heavy matted locks?

verses.sloka: यस्य यज्ञैर्यथोद्दिष्टैर्युक्तो धर्मस्य सञ्चय:।शरीरक्लेशसम्भूतं स धर्मं परिमार्गते ॥ २.९९.३४॥
verses.transliteration: yasya yajñairyathoddiṣṭairyukto dharmasya sañcaya:।śarīrakleśasambhūtaṁ sa dharmaṁ parimārgate ॥ 2.99.34॥

translations.english: That Rama, who in accordance with tradition deserves accredition of religious merit through sacrifices now seeks it through mortification of body.

verses.sloka: चन्दनेन महार्हेण यस्याङ्गमुपसेवितम्।मलेन तस्याङ्गमिदं कथमार्यस्य सेव्यते ॥ २.९९.३५॥
verses.transliteration: candanena mahārheṇa yasyāṅgamupasevitam।malena tasyāṅgamidaṁ kathamāryasya sevyate ॥ 2.99.35॥

translations.english: How is it that the body of my venerable brother which was once smeared with expensive, fragrant sandal paste is now covered with dust?

verses.sloka: मन्निमित्तमिदं दु:खं प्राप्तो राम: सुखोचित:।धिग्जीवितं नृशंसस्य मम लोकविगर्हितम् ॥ २.९९.३६॥
verses.transliteration: mannimittamidaṁ du:khaṁ prāpto rāma: sukhocita:।dhigjīvitaṁ nṛśaṁsasya mama lokavigarhitam ॥ 2.99.36॥

translations.english: It is on my account that Rama who was accustomed to all comforts has fallen into this misfortune. Fie on my life of cruelty which is condemned by the world.

verses.sloka: इत्येवं विलपन् दीन: प्रस्विन्नमुखपङ्कज:।पादावप्राप्य रामस्य पपात भरतो रुदन् ॥ २.९९.३७॥
verses.transliteration: ityevaṁ vilapan dīna: prasvinnamukhapaṅkaja:।pādāvaprāpya rāmasya papāta bharato rudan ॥ 2.99.37॥

translations.english: Thus Bharata lamented in misery and with his lotuslike countenanace sweating before reaching Rama's feet fell down, crying in distress.

verses.sloka: दु:खाभितप्तो भरतो राजपुत्रो महाबल:।उक्त्वार्येति सकृद्दीनं पुनर्नोवाच किञ्चन ॥ २.९९.३८॥
verses.transliteration: du:khābhitapto bharato rājaputro mahābala:।uktvāryeti sakṛddīnaṁ punarnovāca kiñcana ॥ 2.99.38॥

translations.english: Mighty prince Bharata, oppressed with grief, could only say, O Arya (venerable one) And in distress could not speak any more.

verses.sloka: बाष्पापिहितकण्ठश्च प्रेक्ष्य रामं यशस्विनम्।आर्येत्येवाथ संक्रुश्य व्याहर्त्तुं नाशकत्तदा ॥ २.९९.३९॥
verses.transliteration: bāṣpāpihitakaṇṭhaśca prekṣya rāmaṁ yaśasvinam।āryetyevātha saṁkruśya vyāharttuṁ nāśakattadā ॥ 2.99.39॥

translations.english: As he beheld the glorious Rama, with his throat choken with tears, he cried out, O Arya (venerable one) and thereafter, was unable to speak any more.

verses.sloka: शत्रुघ्नश्चापि रामस्य ववन्दे चरणौ रुदन्।तावुभौ स समालिङ्ग्य रामश्चाश्रूण्यवर्त्तयत् ॥ २.९९.४०॥
verses.transliteration: śatrughnaścāpi rāmasya vavande caraṇau rudan।tāvubhau sa samāliṅgya rāmaścāśrūṇyavarttayat ॥ 2.99.40॥

translations.english: Satrughna also prostrated himself at the feet of tearful Rama who embraced both of them.

verses.sloka: तत: सुमन्त्रेण गुहेन चैव समीयतू राजसुतावरण्ये।दिवाकरश्चैव निशाकरश्च यथाम्बरे शुक्रबृहस्पतिभ्याम् ॥ २.९९.४१॥
verses.transliteration: tata: sumantreṇa guhena caiva samīyatū rājasutāvaraṇye।divākaraścaiva niśākaraśca yathāmbare śukrabṛhaspatibhyām ॥ 2.99.41॥

translations.english: Thereafter, princes Rama and Lakshmana joined Sumantra and Guha in the forest like the Sun and the Moon meeting the planets Sukra and Brihaspati in the sky.

verses.sloka: तान् पार्थिवान् वारणयूथपाभान् समागतांस्तत्र महत्यरण्ये।वनौकसस्तेऽपि समीक्ष्य सर्वेप्यश्रूण्यमुञ्चन् प्रविहाय हर्षम् ॥ २.९९.४२ ॥
verses.transliteration: tān pārthivān vāraṇayūthapābhān samāgatāṁstatra mahatyaraṇye।vanaukasaste'pi samīkṣya sarvepyaśrūṇyamuñcan pravihāya harṣam ॥ 2.99.42 ॥

translations.english: On seeing the princes now assembled in the great forest like mighty leaders of elephant herds, inhabitants of the forest had nothing but tears of grief, not joy, to shed. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninetyninth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
